description.value: The study examined differential cortico-limbic activation during voluntary emotion regulation in bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and healthy controls using fMRI.

spans.text: We aimed to distinguish these disorders on the basis of differential activation in cortico-limbic pathways during voluntary emotion regulation.

description.value: A cross-sectional between-subject study of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, and healthy control groups during an emotion regulation fMRI task.

spans.text: In the present study, we sought to distinguish these related disorders on the basis of brain activation during the voluntary regulation of negative affect

The experimental task was adapted from previous studies of emotion regulation in healthy adults.

description.value: Participants voluntarily upregulated, downregulated, or maintained their subjective affect while viewing emotionally negative images.

spans.text: The task required participants to voluntarily upregulate or downregulate their subjective affect while viewing emotionally negative images or maintain their affective response as a comparison condition.
increase
The 10-s regulation periods in each condition (increase, decrease, maintain, neutral) were modeled as separate boxcar regressors

description.value: Participants viewed negative images for 10 seconds after an increase instruction and used cognitive reframing to voluntarily upregulate their subjective negative affect; subjective affect was then rated.

spans.text: Methods to ‘increase' subjective affect were guided by instruction to, for example, imagine that they or a loved one were involved in the depicted situation

The 10-s regulation periods in each condition (increase, decrease, maintain, neutral) were modeled as separate boxcar regressors

description.value: Participants viewed negative images for 10 seconds after a decrease instruction and used cognitive reframing or distancing to voluntarily downregulate their subjective negative affect; subjective affect was then rated.

spans.text: attempts to ‘decrease' subjective affect were guided with instructions to imagine that the situation was not real or that they were a detached observer.

description.value: Participants viewed negative images for 10 seconds after a maintain instruction and were asked to preserve their initial subjective emotional response without alteration; this served as the comparison baseline. Neutral images were also assigned to maintain trials as filler and were not included in the planned analysis.

spans.text: for the ‘maintain' condition, participants were instructed to maintain their initial subjective emotional response to each image, without alteration.

presentation_software.value: Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems, Albany, CA, USA) on a Dell computer running Windows XP

spans.text: The task was programmed and executed using Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems, Albany, CA, USA) on a Dell computer running Windows XP (Microsoft, Redmond, WA, USA).

stimuli.value: Negative and neutral images from the International Affect Picture System (IAPS).

spans.text: The stimulus set comprised 63 negative (for example, scenes of threat or suffering) and 12 neutral (for example, household and working scenes) images selected from the International Affect Picture System (IAPS).
A Lumina MRI-compatible two-button response pad (Cedrus, CA, USA) recorded each response.

instructions.value: For each negative image, participants were instructed to increase, decrease, or maintain their subjective emotional response. Increase and decrease instructions were implemented using cognitive reframing, including reappraisal and/or distancing; participants were instructed to imagine that they or a loved one were involved in the situation to increase affect, or that the situation was not real or that they were detached observers to decrease affect. In the maintain condition, they were instructed to maintain their initial emotional response without alteration.

spans.text: During functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) acquisition, each trial began with an instruction to ‘increase', ‘decrease' or ‘maintain' for 2 s, followed by an image for 10 s.
